newsitem.title: NORWAY: Amoco, BP, Phillips study North Sea cooperation.
newsitem.headline: Amoco, BP, Phillips study North Sea cooperation.

text.p: Amoco Norway Oil Co, British Petroleum Norge and Phillips Petroleum Co are considering a joint cooperation for the running of their operations in the southern North Sea, the operators said on Wednesday.
Amoco operates the Valhall and Hod oilfields, BP the Ula and Gyda developments and Phillips the giant Ekofisk complex.

"Preliminary studies show that significant improvements can be achieved in operations in the southern part of the North Sea. This is possible through comprehensive and long-term cooperation within operations," said a statement from the companies.

"While the need to become more cost effective has been the key driver, the work has also been inspired by the joint government and industry Norsok program to improve the competitiveness of the Norwegian continental shelf."

Amoco, BP and Phillips already have cooperated within logistics and other operations on the five developments. The three have agreed to jointly pursue further studies with a view to reaching an agreement of closer cooperation, they said.
The cooperation will not have any effect on each company's ownership of assets, nor on their accountability as operators.
The companies said they planned to make a decision on any cooperation in January 1997.
